Hi Nina —

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the context on your reconciliation and anomaly-detection pipelines. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clear path forward: 

1) Summary from our demo: Redwood Hosted API can support your real-time enrichment path (single-turn generation + embeddings) and streaming responses for faster UI latency. We showed the Live Chat endpoint and embeddings route for batch similarity.

2) Key questions you flagged for internal alignment:
   - Expected average tokens per request and peak req/s (you said ~6k tokens/request for some templates, 80–120 req/s burst).
   - Data residency + retention for PII in transaction descriptions.
   - Whether Hosted is acceptable initially or you need Private/VPC from day one due to regulatory constraints.

3) Proposed immediate next steps:
   - We can enable a short Hosted evaluation (free trial credit + test API keys) so your engineers can spike integration against your sample data.
   - Dev (cc'd) will reply with the standard Hosted rate limits, endpoint examples (streaming + non-streaming), and a minimal curl example to get started.
   - If after a short trial you need sustained throughput or stricter isolation, we can run a quick qualification for Dedicated capacity or outline Private deployment requirements.

Attachments: Redwood-Hosted-Quickstart.pdf (quickstart guide + example calls)

Would you like us to enable the trial on Monday? If so, share an engineer email for the test key and a small sample payload (sanitized) and Dev will stand up the examples.

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying items before we move to a trial: 

- Volume and tokens: the 6k token average is for long-form reconciliation summaries (once a day per account), but most real-time requests will be ~400–800 tokens. Overall peak traffic for the prototype could hit 100 req/s and may spike to 150+ for short windows.

- Data residency: our legal team prefers EU residency for production, but for an initial proof-of-concept Hosted in US is acceptable if data is not retained beyond 30 days. Can you confirm retention policy for Hosted evaluation?

- Security: we will run the quick PoC on a staging dataset (sanitized) but need to understand audit logging for API calls — are those accessible via the Console for the account?

- Finally, could you share the sample curl and the default rate-limit buckets? We want to ensure the devs can reproduce streaming behavior.

If Hosted looks fine during the trial we may still evaluate Dedicated for predictable throughput and Private/VPC for EU production later.

Appreciate it — can you copy our lead engineer (leo@finbridge.ai) when you send the test keys?

Best,
Nina Kapoor
Head of Platform, FinBridge AI
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Hi Nina —

Quick answers to your specific tech questions and a couple of pragmatic notes for getting a Hosted evaluation running: 

1) Retention & audit logs:
   - Hosted evaluation accounts: default payload/data retention is 30 days for trial accounts (we can configure shorter retention on request).
   - Audit logs and request metadata are visible in the Redwood Console under the "Activity" tab for the account; logs include timestamps, route, model version, token counts, and originating API key id. We can provide a temporary read-only link or export for your legal/security review.

2) Rate limits and throughput (Hosted):
   - Default account tier for trials: 60 requests per second (rps) sustained, with burst capacity up to 180 rps for short windows (couple of minutes) depending on token size.
   - Per-request token concurrency: large requests (6k tokens) will use more CPU/GPU time; for consistent 100+ rps at 6k tokens we typically recommend Dedicated capacity.
   - Per-route quotas: you can create routing rules and per-route quotas via the Console to limit spend.

3) Endpoints & streaming behavior:
   - Non-streaming: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions (json body, model param).
   - Streaming: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streaming-completions — supports SSE and chunked HTTP responses.
   - Embeddings: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings (batching supported up to 512 items per request).

4) Example curl (attached as example-curl.txt) — minimal streaming example using SSE and a single API key. Replace <API_KEY> and model with the one we’ll provide.

5) Next-step recommendations for your spike:
   - We can provision a trial Hosted API key scoped to leo@finbridge.ai for 14 days with 50k free tokens and monitoring access.
   - Run two representative load tests: (a) real-time requests at 400–800 tokens to validate latency and (b) a small batch job for the 6k-token long summaries to measure per-token cost and tail latency.

Attachments: hosted-rate-limits.csv, example-curl.txt

I’ll copy a short checklist into HubSpot (link below) and can run a short sync with your engineering team next week to walk through the curl examples and console.

HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/FB-2026-147

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
